To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) a ranked interpretation of statements, and (ii) user feedback, can be used to improve conflict resolution in integration of metadata from multiple sources.
the FICSR system enables a domain expert to explore the different alternatives for integrating metadata, and to provide feedback to the system to guide the resolution of conflicts and mis-alignments.

the FICSR system (i) provides a ranked interpretation of metadata that enables efficient exploration of alternative resolutions of conflicts and (ii) enables the user to provide expert feedback to resolve the conflicts, and (iii) enables efficient processing of queries and feedback.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(a) the development of a novel approach to conflict-resolution in metadata integration, (b) the development of data structures and algorithms supporting the proposed approach, and (c) the evaluation of the proposed approach in an experimental setting.
the following contributions: 1. We introduce the novel concept of a ranked interpretation for metadata integration, and show its utility in conflict-resolution.

the following research challenges: (1) how to efficiently explore the space of possible worlds and provide feedback to the domain expert about the alternative interpretations, (2) how to efficiently use the expert feedback to resolve the conflicts and to improve the quality of the metadata integration, and (3) how to efficiently process queries and provide the results to the user.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FICSR enables an effective and efficient conflict-resolution process for metadata integration.
the proposed FICSR system is a novel approach for integrating metadata from different data sources.

our approach enables the expert to explore and understand the metadata and the conflicts among different data sources, and to use this understanding to resolve conflicts and to provide feedback to the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by bringing the domain expert in conflict-resolution, we can (a) reduce the number of conflicts to be resolved and (b) resolve conflicts more efficiently and effectively.

we have developed a novel approach for conflict-resolution in the context of integration of metadata from different sources, and we have implemented this approach in the form of a system that supports exploration of alternatives and expert feedback for resolving conflicts during integration.
we present a novel approach for integrating data from different sources that is based on a ranked interpretation of metadata and expert feedback.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the feedback from the domain expert is a critical component for effective conflict-resolution in integration of metadata from different sources, especially when the metadata is not fully specified.

the system feedback, based on the expert feedback and exploration, enables the system to learn about the user’s relevant domain knowledge, which, in turn, can be exploited by the system to improve the quality of the integration process.
, by bringing the expert into the conflict-resolution process, FICSR can help in reducing the overall cost and improving the effectiveness of the process.
